implementation_cost.claim: declared cost of the frozen run
implementation_cost.value: One training-only transition count pass, O(E_train) once. At each of 24 steps/epoch (about 1,023 items/step; 24556 items total), add one exp-map, norm, and pointwise Poincare distance per item: O(BD), no codebook pair expansion. At 3000 epochs the extra work is 24*3000*B pointwise distances; expected small relative to encoder and codebook assignment, with no additional training run.

prior_work.claim: proposal novelty statement
prior_work.value: It replaces pairwise successor clustering with a scalar, item-specific radial target computed from continuation uncertainty. Unlike unchanged Euclidean RQ-VAE plus a behavior suffix, the target is a Poincare radius of the exact encoder representation consumed by quantization; unlike generic hyperbolic RQ-VAE, the radius is set by observed training-only branching.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From adjacent timestamp-ordered events within each training user sequence only, build F_i and m_i. For each i, choose p by maximum successor-set Jaccard overlap; choose n with empty intersection and m_n at least the train-item median, nearest to i under frozen baseline Euclidean embeddings. Freeze this deterministic pair table.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: Pair mining and all medians use training transitions and the already frozen baseline Stage2 embeddings only. Validation/test interactions, labels and scores are never read during pair construction, loss computation, or SID export; Stage3 evaluation consumes the frozen candidate SIDs.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Keep the hyperbolic ranking computation but permute p_i across item IDs using the fixed seed, breaking the correspondence; the behavior term no longer ranks true successor overlaps.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use the actual train-only p_i ordering and Poincare geodesic distances as specified; this is the sole trained candidate, with no ablation arm.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Keep the exact train pairs, targets, margin and schedules, but replace d_c with Euclidean ||h_i−h_j||₂ and remove exp/log maps.
ideas.behavior_computation: Count consecutive distinct item events per user in the Stage0 training parquet only; aggregate n_ij, destination q, and p_i once before training. No validation/test rows are read.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed next-item transition distributions and their pairwise Jensen–Shannon overlap.
ideas.cost_estimate: One-time train graph build O(E); per step O(BD) encoder-to-ball mapping and O(BD) geodesic triplet calculations for B≤4096 anchors (at most 4096 triplets), versus baseline embedding/quantization O(BD). At 24 steps/epoch × 3000 epochs = 72,000 steps, adds 72,000 bounded triplet batches; expected modest arithmetic overhead, no extra model or data pass beyond one train-only graph build and the allowed warmup-scale estimate.
ideas.coupling_equation: L_fork=E_{s_ik>s_il} softplus((d_c(z_i,z_k)−d_c(z_i,z_l)+m)/τ); s_ik=1−JS(p_i,p_k)/log 2. Behavior determines pair ordering; curved distance is the scored quantity.
ideas.coupling_path: Train-only successor-distribution overlap orders sampled item pairs; that order sets which encoder representations must be geodesically nearer/farther, and the resulting gradients update the same encoder representation consumed by the quantizer.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: The mechanism is worth keeping if the single frozen Stage3 run has test Recall@10 > 0.065; supporting observations are changed encoder gradients and more predictable successor ranking from SID prefixes, recorded only as diagnostics, never gates.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: The pre-quantization encoder output is mapped to the ball; the training-only pairwise successor-ranking objective differentiates through Poincare distance before ordinary RQ-VAE quantization.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball distance d_c(x,y)=2/sqrt(c) atanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)⊕_c y||), with negative curvature −c; log/exp mapping from encoder tangent output to ball.
ideas.key_change: From train-only transitions, form smoothed successor distributions and sample item pairs; train the encoder to order their Poincare distances according to successor-distribution overlap, with an adaptive margin derived from the batch's distance scale. Retain the canonical reconstruction and quantization losses.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Graph, frequency smoothing, pair sampler, scale statistics and triplets are functions only of the training parquet and train embeddings; freeze the resulting graph before fitting, and construct/export SIDs without validation or test interactions.
ideas.motivation: A next-item code should preserve which items are interchangeable within a user's observed branching future, while separating items whose successor sets diverge; raw semantic reconstruction does not express this predictive distinction.
ideas.novelty: Unlike successor co-occurrence attraction or a per-item radial shell target, this uses the *ranked overlap of successor distributions* as a pair-specific target and applies it directly to geodesic distances between the encoder representations that feed the RQ quantizer.
ideas.observables: Encoder gradients and learned item vectors should change; SID assignments and prefix-level successor-rank predictability may change. Record these and Stage3 test Recall@10; only Recall@10 > 0.065 is success.

rebuttal.change: Add a pre-registered matched Euclidean comparison: hold the train-only triplets, encoder, initialization, optimizer, batch order, margin and temperature schedule, and loss-coefficient schedule fixed; use the same detached distance-scale and loss-ratio estimates in both arms, with the Euclidean arm replacing only the Poincaré mapping and distance by Euclidean distance on the same encoder outputs. Specify behavior-off as a fixed seeded permutation of successor profiles with geometry retained, geometry-off as the matched Euclidean replacement with true profiles retained, and both-on as true profiles with Poincaré distance. Compare both-on against geometry-off under the same single-run success criterion; this makes curved-geometry value falsifiable rather than inferred from adaptive scaling or normalization.
rebuttal.remaining: A matched specification cannot establish that curvature will outperform Euclidean ranking; that remains an empirical uncertainty, and a single run cannot quantify seed variability.
rebuttal.unchanged: The successor-overlap-ranked triplet mechanism, train-only data boundary, Poincaré ranking in the candidate, and canonical reconstruction and quantization losses.
rebuttal.why: The comparison isolates geometry while making both switch controls operational and preventing either adaptive scale or loss-ratio normalization from being mistaken for evidence that curvature adds value.

rejected_ideas.reason: out of scope: ablation_geometry_off does not say what replaces the curve

risks: Sparse transition rows make JS noisy; too many near-tied successor distributions weaken triplet signal; hyperbolic distance scale may be dominated by norm rather than angle; the automatically normalized loss can still conflict with reconstruction.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp ball norm below (1−1e−5)/sqrt(c); clamp atanh argument to 1−1e−6; add ε=1e−8 to row denominators, JS logs and MAD; skip anchors without two distinct successor-overlap ranks; compute geometry/loss in float32 under mixed precision; detach scale and λ estimates; clip gradients with baseline norm 1.0.
ideas.spec_equations: Build p_i; per step encode h_i, map z_i=exp^c_0(h_i); draw train-derived (i,k,l), where s_ik>s_il; compute batch m,τ from detached valid distances; L=L_RQVAE+λ(t)L_fork. λ(t)=EMA(L_RQVAE)/EMA(L_fork) during epochs 1–50, then freeze at epoch 50. Geometry-off and behavior-off switches select the alternatives described above without changing any other code path.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: train-only transition counts, current item embeddings and encoder, sampled item-index triplets. Output: scalar coupled loss and gradients to encoder; standard quantizer then emits unchanged-format three-level SIDs.

specification.text: Let n_ij be train-event transitions i→j. Define p_i(j)=(n_ij+α q(j))/(n_i+α), where q is train-only destination frequency normalized and α=1. For sampled pair (i,k), s_ik=1−JS(p_i,p_k)/log 2. Let z_i be the pre-quantization encoder output mapped to the ball, and d_c its Poincare distance, c=1/(median_batch ||h||²+ε) (fixed after an initial train-only encoder pass, clipped only to the ball-safe range). For triplets (i,k,l) ordered so s_ik>s_il, use Lfork=softplus((d_c(z_i,z_k)−d_c(z_i,z_l)+m)/τ), m=median of positive batch geodesic distances, τ=median absolute deviation of those distances (ε floor). Pair/triplet sampling is deterministic from seed 42 and train graph; take at most one triplet per anchor per step. Add Lfork with coefficient set to the ratio of baseline reconstruction-loss EMA to fork-loss EMA over the first 50 warmup epochs (stop-gradient; then freeze), avoiding a tuned weight.

ideas.title: Successor-fork rank supervision through a hyperbolic geodesic margin
ideas.unresolved_objection: A matched specification cannot establish that curvature will outperform Euclidean ranking; that remains an empirical uncertainty, and a single run cannot quantify seed variability.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Preserve curvature and radial penalty, but replace u_i by a fixed seeded permutation across item IDs, destroying the fanout-to-radius mapping.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use each item's actual train-only fanout to set inverse-hyperbolic-volume radius and penalize its Poincare origin distance; this is the sole candidate run, not a trained ablation.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Preserve fanout targets and schedules, but use Euclidean radius ||h_i|| and a Euclidean volume law V(r)∝r^d (equivalently radius target transformed from the same volume quantile); remove ball maps and geodesic distance.
ideas.behavior_computation: For each user's chronologically ordered Stage0 training events, count adjacent transitions i→j, then count distinct destinations j per source item i; use log1p and robust train-item median/IQR normalization. Validation/test transitions are excluded.
ideas.behavior_signal: Per-item number of distinct observed immediate successors (fanout), derived from directed train-only user transitions.
ideas.cost_estimate: One-time train graph O(E), one encoder-only warmup statistics pass O(24556D), and a small (e.g. 256-node) scalar volume lookup table. Each of 72,000 steps adds one norm/radius per item, O(BD), and scalar squared error; no pairwise matrix. Four-card, 24-step × 3000-epoch schedule unchanged; added work is negligible relative to baseline encoder and quantizer.
ideas.coupling_equation: u_i=robustnorm(log(1+outdegree_train(i))); r_i=V_c^{-1}(V_c(r_0)e^{κu_i}); L_rad=mean_i (1+|u_i|)^{-1}[d_c(0,z_i)−r_i]^2. The behavior signal chooses r_i and curved geometry measures the prediction error.
ideas.coupling_path: Each item's train-only successor fanout determines its target volume/radius; the hyperbolic radial error on the same encoder point the quantizer consumes produces gradients that alter its SID assignment.

ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If fanout hierarchy matters to generation, placing high-fanout items at radii implied by hyperbolic volume growth will reorganize RQ coarse prefixes in a way that helps generation; keep only if the single frozen Stage3 test Recall@10 exceeds 0.065. Record radius/fanout correlation, SID changes and prefix successor predictability diagnostically, not as admission criteria.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Before residual quantization, the encoder point is mapped into the Poincare ball; the training penalty matches its geodesic radius to a branching-calibrated radius obtained through inverse hyperbolic volume.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare origin distance d_c(0,z)=2/sqrt(c) atanh(sqrt(c)||z||), and the negative-curvature ball-volume law V_c(r)∝∫sinh(√c r)^{d−1}dr with curvature −c.
ideas.key_change: Estimate each item's effective successor branching, map it monotonically to a target hyperbolic radius using the volume-growth law, and penalize the squared geodesic radial discrepancy between that target and the encoder point. This is a radial-only fork signal, distinct from pairwise angular/coherence or codebook assignment mechanisms.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Fanout and all normalization statistics come only from the training parquet; warmup encoder radii use only the frozen training-item embedding matrix. No user interactions from validation/test are read for fitting, radius targets, quantization or SID export.
ideas.motivation: Items that initiate many distinct future choices behave like branching hubs, while items with few futures occupy narrower predictive roles; encoding this distinction in the hierarchy could make the quantizer's coarse prefixes useful for next-item generation.
ideas.novelty: This is not a shell-geometry assignment rule or an independent behavior regularizer: train-only successor fanout sets a per-item target *hyperbolic ball volume*, and inverse volume geometry directly calibrates the encoder radius the RQ-VAE quantizer receives.
ideas.observables: Encoder norms/radii should track train fanout in hyperbolic-radius units; SID levels/prefix assignment and prefix successor predictability may change. Stage3 test Recall@10 > 0.065 is the sole keep criterion.
risks: Degree is a blunt branching proxy and may measure exposure/popularity; the radial target may consume representational capacity or distort semantic reconstruction; inverse-volume saturation near the ball boundary requires careful bounded lookup; no repeated seed can separate effect from seed noise.
ideas.safeguards: Restrict ||z||≤(1−1e−5)/sqrt(c); clamp inverse-table query to its endpoint range; use float64 for lookup table construction and float32 interpolation/training; set ε=1e−8 for normalization and volume; use stable log-sinh evaluation; stop gradients through target radii, c, quantiles and λ; clip gradients at baseline norm 1.0; log fraction of clipped targets/radii without using it as a gate.
ideas.spec_equations: Build b_i and u_i from train edges. During warmup estimate c, r_0, r_min, r_max; build monotone table for V_c and inverse. At each step, z_i=exp^c_0(h_i), r_i=V_c^{-1}(V_c(r_0)e^{κu_i}), L=L_RQVAE+λ(t)mean_i(d_c(0,z_i)−r_i)^2/(1+|u_i|). Estimate λ by detached EMA loss ratio in epochs 1–50, freeze thereafter. Geometry-off replaces ball radius and V_c with Euclidean norm and Euclidean volume; behavior-off permutes u.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: train transition edge counts/fanout, encoder outputs for batch items, curvature and warmup radius statistics. Outputs: scalar radial loss/encoder gradients and ordinary RQ quantizer output SIDs.

specification.text: From train transitions define smoothed outgoing degree b_i=log(1+|{j:n_ij>0}|) and normalize u_i=(b_i−median(b))/(IQR(b)+ε), clipped to [−1,1]. For curvature −c with c fixed to 1/(median_i ||h_i||²+ε), compute hyperbolic d-dimensional ball volume V_c(r)=|S^{d−1}|∫_0^r (sinh(√c t)/√c)^{d−1}dt. Set target radius r_i=V_c^{-1}(V_c(r_0) exp(κ u_i)), where r_0=median current geodesic radius and κ=log(V_c(r_max)/V_c(r_min))/2, r_min/r_max are the 10th/90th percentiles of train-only encoder radii from the warmup pass. Use a lookup table with monotone interpolation for inverse volume. Lrad=mean_i w_i(d_c(0,z_i)−r_i)^2, with w_i=1/(1+|u_i|) so sparse extremes cannot dominate; coefficient λ=baseline reconstruction-loss EMA / Lrad EMA measured during epochs 1–50 and then frozen.

ideas.title: Successor-fanout calibrated hyperbolic radial supervision

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Keep Poincare distance and margin but replace training-derived triples with a deterministic label-free identity/no-pair set, making Lfork=0; this is a specification switch, not a trained arm.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use the frozen training-derived fork triples and Poincare geodesic triplet loss for the one candidate, with exactly 3000 Stage2 epochs on four cards, frozen Stage3 protocol and no early stopping.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Keep the exact frozen triples, pair sampler, mu and gamma but replace d_P,c(z_i,z_j) with Euclidean ||z_i-z_j||₂; this is a specification switch, not a trained arm.
ideas.behavior_computation: From adjacent timestamp-ordered events within each training user sequence only, build F_i and m_i. For each i, choose p by maximum successor-set Jaccard overlap; choose n with empty intersection and m_n at least the train-item median, nearest to i under frozen baseline Euclidean embeddings. Freeze this deterministic pair table.
ideas.behavior_signal: Training-only shared-successor positive pairs and popularity-gated disjoint-successor negatives.
ideas.cost_estimate: Precompute sparse F_i, degrees, valid pairs and baseline nearest eligible negatives once: O(E_train) storage and graph work; one triplet distance and hinge per valid anchor per step, O(Bd) extra, B≈1024 at 24556 items/24 steps. Over 24 steps/epoch × 3000 epochs, adds at most 3 Poincare distances/item/step in the encoder batch, negligible versus codebook assignment; no second model or additional run.
ideas.coupling_equation: Lfork=E_[i,p,n](max(0,d_P,c(z_i,z_p)-d_P,c(z_i,z_n)+mu)); L=L_RQVAE+gamma Lfork, where the fork-derived triples determine the arguments of both curved distances.
ideas.coupling_path: Training-only fork pairs select anchor-positive-negative triples; the Poincare distance differences determine the hinge and encoder gradients; the gradients change pre-quantizer embeddings, code assignments and exported SIDs.

ideas.hyperbolic_location: Auxiliary gradient term on the encoder's pre-quantization latent z_i; this same z_i enters the unchanged RQ quantizer, so the curved gradient changes the learned representation and resulting SID assignments.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Squared-curvature Poincare geodesic distance d_P,c with fixed negative sectional curvature -c, used in an explicit triplet ranking hinge.
ideas.key_change: Form anchor-positive pairs from items with shared successors and anchor-negative pairs from high-exposure items with disjoint successors; apply a scale-normalized Poincare geodesic ranking loss to their encoder embeddings before RQ quantization, added to the existing objective with a coefficient derived from baseline reconstruction-loss scale.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Pair mining and all medians use training transitions and the already frozen baseline Stage2 embeddings only. Validation/test interactions, labels and scores are never read during pair construction, loss computation, or SID export; Stage3 evaluation consumes the frozen candidate SIDs.
ideas.motivation: Content reconstruction can place behaviorally incompatible items close together even when their likely next-item branches differ, making generative SID prefixes ambiguous for next-item decoding.
ideas.novelty: This uses a fixed training-only pair sampler and a Poincare triplet margin on encoder outputs, rather than radial/angular target supervision, a behavior-conditioned transform, or behavior-weighted code assignment. The behavior-derived pair controls which items enter the curved geometric comparison, and its gradient flows into the exact pre-quantizer representation used to make SIDs.
ideas.observables: Margin satisfaction, encoder gradient norms, SID assignments/prefixes for sampled fork pairs, and train-only fork predictability are recorded; only frozen Stage3 test Recall@10 >0.065 judges the candidate.
risks: Hard negatives may encode popularity rather than genuine incompatibility; selecting nearest baseline embeddings can create false negatives; sparse successor sets yield few valid triplets; the loss may compete with reconstruction or be absorbed by the quantizer. Geometry could add no benefit over Euclidean distances.
ideas.safeguards: Exclude empty successor sets and self-pairs; require positive overlap/disjointness exactly as specified; use fixed candidate set and deterministic tie-breaking. Clamp Poincare norms to (1-eps)/sqrt(c), atanh inputs to 1-eps; compute maps/distances and loss scaling in float32 with stable small-norm limits. If no valid pairs, set gamma=0 and log that condition (mechanism has no signal). Derive mu and gamma once from baseline initialization; do not retune or use validation/test outcomes.
ideas.spec_equations: F_i={j:Σ_{u,t in train}1[x_ut=i,x_u,t+1=j]>0}, m_i=Σ_j n_ij. p_i=argmax_{p≠i}|F_i∩F_p|/(|F_i∪F_p|+eps), requiring nonempty intersection. n_i=argmin_{n:F_i∩F_n=∅,m_n≥median(m)}||z_i^base-z_n^base||₂. mu=median_{valid i}[d_P,c(z_i^base,z_p^base),d_P,c(z_i^base,z_n^base)] (pooled distances). h_i=max(0,d_P,c(z_i,z_p)-d_P,c(z_i,z_n)+mu). gamma=median_i Lrec_i^base / median_{valid i,h_i^base>0}h_i^base, with gamma=0 if denominator/valid set empty. Train L=L_RQVAE+gamma mean_i h_i. Re-sample nothing: fixed triples for every epoch.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: training-only event sequences, frozen baseline encoder embeddings and per-item reconstruction losses, candidate encoder latent z_i, and curvature c. Output: fork loss and gradients to encoder; the existing quantizer returns the final SID sequence.

specification.text: From train-only transitions define F_i and degree m_i=Σ_j n_ij. For each anchor i, positive p is the shared-successor item maximizing |F_i∩F_p|/(|F_i∪F_p|+eps); negative n is among items with F_i∩F_n=∅ and m_n≥median(m), chosen as nearest baseline Euclidean embedding to avoid trivial negatives. Define Lfork=mean[max(0, d_P,c(z_i,z_p)-d_P,c(z_i,z_n)+mu)] with mu=median training Poincare distance at baseline initialization. Let gamma=median per-item baseline reconstruction loss / median per-item nonzero triplet hinge at initialization (or zero if no valid triplets). Optimize Lbase+gamma Lfork, with deterministic one positive/negative per valid anchor per epoch from fixed train graph. Existing hard quantization and decoder unchanged.

ideas.title: Train encoder separation by a successor-fork geodesic margin

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set all t_i to the training-set median target, retaining the identical curved distance and pathway; this removes item-specific behavior supervision. This switch exists for comparison but is not trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use the per-item training successor-entropy target and curvature -1 Poincare exp maps/distance as specified. Train exactly this single candidate once; no ablation arm is run.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Replace both exp maps and d_B by their tangent-space Euclidean counterparts, retaining t_i, R, and the same normalized objective. This switch exists for comparison but is not trained in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From training split user sequences, count each adjacent pair (i,j), form each source's empirical successor distribution and normalized entropy; no validation/test sequences or held-out interactions are read.
ideas.behavior_signal: Per-item normalized entropy of directed next-item outcomes (successor branching).
ideas.cost_estimate: One training-only transition count pass, O(E_train) once. At each of 24 steps/epoch (about 1,023 items/step; 24556 items total), add one exp-map, norm, and pointwise Poincare distance per item: O(BD), no codebook pair expansion. At 3000 epochs the extra work is 24*3000*B pointwise distances; expected small relative to encoder and codebook assignment, with no additional training run.
ideas.coupling_equation: L_fork=mean_i [ w_i d_B^2(exp_o^c(z_i), exp_o^c(t_i R u_i)) ], where w_i=1 and t_i is the training-only normalized successor-entropy target.
ideas.coupling_path: Training successor entropy determines a target radius, and the distance from the exp-mapped encoder latent to that target generates gradients on the pre-quantization latent; removing entropy removes item-specific targets, while replacing the geodesic with Euclidean distance removes the curved radial geometry.

evidence_revision.evidence_note: Positive row scalar leaves every arg-min unchanged: True. Codeword-dependent weight moved False of the top-1; denominator UNKNOWN.
evidence_revision.revision: The proposal is limited to supervising latent radius; it does not claim this radial signal changes quantized assignments or survives quantization, because the evidence shows a positive row scalar leaves arg-min assignments unchanged.
evidence_revision.withdrawn: The claim that the radial gradients will move assignments or that the signal survives quantization.

ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Worth keeping only if training-only branching predicts useful next-item uncertainty and the radial gradients move encoder latents in a way that survives quantization; observe changed latent radii/SID assignments and, decisively, frozen Stage3 test Recall@10 > 0.065. Diagnostics are descriptive only.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Auxiliary supervision on the encoder output immediately before RQ-VAE quantization; its gradients update that same encoder representation read by the quantizer.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball exp map at the origin and squared geodesic distance d_B^2 for curvature -c, c=1.
ideas.key_change: From training-only outgoing transition entropy, map each item's normalized branch entropy to a target Poincare radius and penalize the squared geodesic distance between that radial target and the encoded item. Apply the penalty to the pre-quantization latent after exp-map, alongside the unchanged canonical reconstruction/RQ-VAE objective.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition table and entropy targets are computed once from the training split only; validation/test data are unavailable to target construction, normalization, or model updates. Stage3 uses the resulting frozen SIDs under the prescribed protocol.
ideas.motivation: An item with many distinct next-item outcomes represents a broad behavioral fork, while a low-branching item has a more predictable continuation; semantic IDs should expose this difference in their coarse latent representation.
ideas.novelty: It replaces pairwise successor clustering with a scalar, item-specific radial target computed from continuation uncertainty. Unlike unchanged Euclidean RQ-VAE plus a behavior suffix, the target is a Poincare radius of the exact encoder representation consumed by quantization; unlike generic hyperbolic RQ-VAE, the radius is set by observed training-only branching.
ideas.observables: With the full mechanism, radial latent norms and resulting SID assignments should become associated with training-only branching, while Stage3 test Recall@10 is the sole keep/reject outcome; target >0.065.
risks: Branch entropy may be a popularity or data-frequency proxy rather than stable user intent; the quantizer may erase the radial signal; small/no-outdegree items have weak supervision; per-batch radius calibration can be noisy.
ideas.safeguards: Float32 geometry; clamp tangent norms below (1-eps)/sqrt(c) before exp-map; clamp Poincare distance denominators and acosh/atanh arguments; eps=machine-safe 1e-6; skip/zero-target no-outdegree items; if q95<=q05 set all t_i to 0; detach R and loss-scale estimates; assert finite losses/gradients. Curvature c=1 is a documented fixed default, not tuned.
ideas.spec_equations: For item i, n_ij=count_train(i->j), p_ij=n_ij/(sum_j n_ij+eps), h_i=-sum_j p_ij log(p_ij+eps), q_i=h_i/log(max(2,d_i)) if d_i>=2 else 0. Normalize q_i by training-item q05,q95 to t_i in [0,1]. z_i=Encoder(x_i); u_i=z_i/(||z_i||+eps); R=stopgrad(percentile95_batch(||z||)); y_i=exp_o^c(t_i R u_i); v_i=exp_o^c(z_i). Optimize canonical L_RQVAE plus scale-normalized mean d_B(v_i,y_i)^2. Use the existing training split and canonical 3000-epoch schedule.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are training content embedding x_i, training-only transition count table, and encoder latent z_i; output is scalar auxiliary loss and its gradients into z_i/encoder. It does not change the RQ-VAE codebook interface or Stage3 input format.

specification.text: Count directed adjacent item pairs in training user sequences only: n_ij. Define p(j|i)=n_ij/sum_j n_ij and h_i=-sum_j p(j|i)log p(j|i), with h_i=0 for no outgoing edges. Set q_i=h_i/log(max(2,d_i)), where d_i is the number of distinct successors (and q_i=0 when d_i<2). On a training-only item set, let q05 and q95 be empirical 5th/95th percentiles; set t_i=clip((q_i-q05)/(q95-q05+eps),0,1). With fixed c=1 negative curvature, radial target y_i=exp_o^c((t_i R)u_i), where u_i=z_i/(||z_i||+eps), R is the empirical 95th percentile of ||z|| over the current training minibatch, detached from gradients. Minimize L=L_RQVAE+mean_i d_B^2(exp_o^c(z_i),y_i); unit coefficient after each term is divided by its detached minibatch mean (clamped below by eps). This defines scale without a sweep.

ideas.title: Successor-branch radial supervision by Poincare geodesic distance

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set a_i=0 and replace p_ij barycenter with no behavioral target, yielding zero auxiliary loss while preserving baseline RQ-VAE. This switch exists in code but is not trained this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use training-only directed probabilities and entropy weights with Poincare barycenters, geodesic midpoint, and Poincare distance. This is the sole candidate trained once; no ablation arm is run.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Use Euclidean weighted successor barycenter, Euclidean midpoint (x_i+b_i)/2 and squared Euclidean distance, with all same edges and a_i. This switch exists in code but is not trained this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From adjacent item pairs in training user sequences only, count n_ij, normalize each source row to p(j|i), and calculate entropy normalized by log distinct outdegree; minibatch barycenters renormalize only over included training successors.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed next-item transition distribution and its normalized successor entropy.
ideas.cost_estimate: Precompute sparse directed counts once in O(E_train). Per step on about 1,023 of 24,556 items, gather sparse successor edges and perform exp/log maps and one barycenter plus midpoint per eligible source: O(E_B D), where E_B is the number of sampled observed outgoing edges, bounded by the training graph's sparse minibatch edges; no all-pairs item matrix. 24 steps/epoch for 3000 epochs; added edge-wise geometry may be noticeable but remains sparse, with no extra run.
ideas.coupling_equation: L_cont=mean_i [a_i d_B^2(x_i, exp_{x_i}(0.5 log_{x_i}( exp_o(sum_j p_ij log_o(x_j)) )))], where x_k=exp_o(z_k) and a_i is normalized training successor entropy.
ideas.coupling_path: Training transition probabilities construct a successor barycenter in the Poincare ball; branching entropy gates the geodesic-midpoint pull on the same encoded point. Without the transition signal there is no barycenter, and with Euclidean geometry the barycenter/midpoint computation and distance are replaced, changing that same gradient path.

evidence_revision.evidence_note: A positive row scalar left every arg-min unchanged (measured: True); a codeword-dependent weight moved False of the top-1 assignments. No measurement was provided showing that this geodesic-midpoint mechanism changes assignments.
evidence_revision.revision: Retain the specified successor-conditioned geodesic-midpoint regularizer only as a latent-organization hypothesis; the probe gives no support that this mechanism changes top-1 assignments, so no assignment-change claim is made
evidence_revision.withdrawn: The claim or implication that this proposal will move assignments or produce changed assignments

ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Worth keeping if shared continuations identify behaviorally interchangeable items and the entropy-weighted curved midpoint regularizes their latent organization without blurring content distinctions; observe training-only successor alignment and changed assignments, but decide only by Stage3 test Recall@10 > 0.065.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: The auxiliary target construction and loss on the encoder's pre-quantization latents; gradients feed directly into the latent representations consumed by the baseline quantizer.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare exp/log maps and the geodesic midpoint obtained by exp_x(0.5 log_x(y)) under fixed curvature -1; distance is Poincare geodesic distance.
ideas.key_change: For each training item, form a weighted Fréchet-style barycenter of its successors' Poincare points and pull its encoded point toward the geodesic midpoint between its current point and that continuation barycenter. Weight this pull by the source's normalized branching uncertainty, so branching controls how strongly the item is placed between its own semantic location and its behavioral continuation.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Both transition rows and entropy scaling quantiles are built exclusively from training interactions; the per-step barycenter accesses only training item IDs and current model latents. Validation/test interactions are never loaded into SID construction or optimization.
ideas.motivation: Items that lead into the same downstream item can represent alternative entry points into a common continuation; their SIDs should retain that behavioral substitutability without collapsing every item with broad branching into one cluster.
ideas.novelty: The mechanism supervises a curved, directed predecessor-to-successor barycentric relation, rather than assigning behavior-weighted codewords, running behavior Sinkhorn, or applying an independent behavior loss to an unrelated representation. It couples the successor structure to a Poincare geodesic midpoint target on the quantizer's own latent.
ideas.observables: The on-mechanism should alter encoder gradients and SIDs in proportion to directed continuation barycenters; record latent/assignment and successor-alignment diagnostics, never as admission gates. Stage3 test Recall@10 must exceed 0.065 to retain.
risks: A midpoint toward popular successors can over-associate unrelated sources; minibatches may omit most successors and produce noisy barycenters; high-entropy sources may receive a diffuse, unhelpful target; curvature may add cost or unstable gradients.
ideas.safeguards: Float32 manifold arithmetic; project ball points to radius (1-eps)/sqrt(c); clamp norms and log/atanh/acosh arguments; eps=1e-6; renormalize minibatch successor weights safely; skip empty rows; stop-gradient the auxiliary-loss scale; cap each source's included edge list at its observed sparse row length (no dense expansion); assert finite values. Use c=1 documented default.
ideas.spec_equations: p_ij=n_ij/(sum_k n_ik+eps); h_i=-sum_j p_ij log(p_ij+eps); q_i=h_i/log(max(2,d_i)); scale q to a_i in [0,1] by train-item 5th/95th quantiles. For included successors J_i, p'_ij=p_ij/(sum_{k in J_i}p_ik+eps), x_k=exp_o^c(z_k), b_i=exp_o^c(sum_{j in J_i}p'_ij log_o^c(x_j)), m_i=exp_{x_i}^c(0.5 log_{x_i}^c(b_i)); optimize L_RQVAE plus normalized mean a_i d_B^2(x_i,m_i). Fixed c=1; no constant sweep.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are current minibatch encoder latents, sparse training-only directed transition rows, and train-derived entropy quantiles. Output is scalar auxiliary loss and gradients to all included source/successor latents; quantizer and downstream SID interface remain unchanged.

specification.text: Build train-only directed counts n_ij and successor probabilities p_ij as in the first idea. For each minibatch source i with at least one observed successor represented in the minibatch, map current successor latents z_j to Poincare points x_j=exp_o^c(z_j), then compute a tangent-space barycenter b_i=exp_o^c(sum_j p_ij log_o^c(x_j)) using only observed successors (renormalize p over included successors). Define m_i as the Poincare geodesic midpoint between x_i=exp_o^c(z_i) and b_i, computed m_i=exp_{x_i}(0.5 log_{x_i}(b_i)). Let a_i be normalized successor entropy in [0,1] using training-set q05/q95. Minimize L=L_RQVAE+mean_i a_i*d_B^2(x_i,m_i), with the auxiliary term divided by its detached minibatch mean when positive. No-successor or absent-successor items contribute zero. This supplies a unit-free scale and uses fixed c=1.

ideas.title: Shared-successor angular attraction with branch-calibrated hyperbolic geodesics

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: In code only, behavior_on=False sets S_ij=b_i=0, so g_i^l=0 while retaining Poincare assignment. Do not train this arm.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The single formal candidate uses training-derived S,b and Poincare Exp/distance together as in the coupling equation. Train only this arm once under the frozen recipe.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: In code only, geometry_on=False uses identity mapping and squared Euclidean assignment distance on the same behavior-shifted vector. Do not train this arm.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only, form N(i) from observed directed anchor→next-item pairs; compute top-k Jaccard overlaps S_ij and b_i as specified. Do not use valid/test sequences, labels, or co-occurrence statistics.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed successor-set overlap, weighted by successor branching.
ideas.cost_estimate: Precompute sparse top-k overlap once from 24,556 training items; memory O(E_k), where E_k is retained directed neighbour count. Per step, B=4096 item lookups plus sparse gather O(BkD), then B×K Poincare distances per layer, the same asymptotic assignment cost as the baseline and a modest distance/map overhead; 24 steps/epoch × 3000 epochs = 72,000 steps, no extra training pass or run.
ideas.coupling_equation: q_i^l=argmin_k d_c(Exp_0^c(r_i^l+g_i^l), Exp_0^c(c_k^l))^2, where g_i^l=(b_i/(1+b_i))W_l[Σ_j S_ij e_j/(Σ_j S_ij+eps)]; S,b are training behaviour and d_c,Exp are curved operations.
ideas.coupling_path: The train-only successor-overlap aggregate shifts the representation before Exp_0^c; the resulting Poincare distance selects the code and supplies the quantization gradient. Removing behaviour removes the shift; replacing curved maps/distance changes that assignment computation.

evidence_revision.answers: answers the behavior-dependency gap: a positive row scalar preserves arg-min, and the tested codeword-dependent weight did not move top-1
evidence_revision.evidence_note: Positive row scalar leaves every arg-min unchanged (measured: True); codeword-dependent weight moved 0 top-1 assignments (measured: False)
evidence_revision.revision: The proposal no longer claims that its behavior-dependent weighting moves assignments or makes codes branch-consistent; the available probe does not establish that the specified tangent transport changes top-1 assignments, so any such effect remains unsupported
evidence_revision.withdrawn: The claim that the coupled successor signal and curved distance change assignments toward branch-consistent codes

ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If alternatives sharing observed successor context should have nearby usable codes, the coupled tangent shift will change assignments and encoder/codebook gradients toward branch-consistent codes, yielding Stage3 test Recall@10 > 0.065. Record assignment changes, successor-neighbour retrieval and test Recall; behaviour diagnostics are descriptive only.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In each residual-quantization layer, immediately before nearest-code assignment, where the adjusted representation, code locations and assignment gradient are computed.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare exponential map Exp_0^c and Poincare distance d_c at fixed negative curvature -c, c=1.
ideas.key_change: Precompute a sparse successor-overlap vector for each item. At each quantization layer, add that vector (scaled by the item's branch ambiguity) to the current tangent residual, map the result into a fixed-curvature Poincare ball, and select the code by Poincare distance; reconstruction/commitment gradients pass through this same transformed point.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Build and freeze the sparse S table exclusively from Stage2 training interactions before optimization. Every item receives a deterministic global SID; validation/test interactions are unavailable to the constructor and are used only by the frozen Stage3 evaluation protocol.
ideas.motivation: Items reached from the same training prefix often serve a shared user-interest branch; vanilla reconstruction can place those alternatives in unrelated directions, making their codes weakly useful for next-item generation.
ideas.novelty: Rather than adding a separate behaviour loss to the encoder, train-only successor overlap supplies the target tangent direction used by a Poincare-geodesic assignment cost. This is a local, branch-conditioned transport of the representation the quantizer actually reads, not a Euclidean suffix or a hyperbolic-only regularizer.
ideas.observables: Changed SID assignments and codebook/encoder update directions for high-overlap branches; changed predictability of held-out training prefixes from SID prefixes; final Stage3 test Recall@10 is the judgement.
risks: Sparse Jaccard overlap may be noisy for rare items; the tangent shift can overwhelm reconstruction despite its bounded coefficient; ambiguity may correlate with popularity rather than true branching; fixed curvature may add cost without useful geometry.
ideas.safeguards: Add eps=machine epsilon for empty sets/normalization; empty neighbourhood means g=0. Clip tangent norms only to the analytic ball-domain limit (1-1e-5)/sqrt(c) before Exp; project code points to same open ball; clamp acosh arguments to >=1+machine epsilon; compute distances in float32 under AMP; skip non-finite overlap rows and log counts. No validation-derived statistics or tuned clipping/temperature.
ideas.spec_equations: (1) From train edges: N(i)={j:(i,j) observed}; S_ij=Jaccard(N(i),N(j)), retain top min(8,degree(i)); b_i=Σ_j S_ij log(1+|N(j)|). (2) m_i=Σ_j S_ij e_j/(Σ_j S_ij+eps); g_i^l=b_i/(1+b_i) W_l m_i. (3) x_i^l=Exp_0^1(r_i^l+g_i^l); q_i^l=argmin_k d_{-1}(x_i^l,Exp_0^1(c_k^l))². Apply standard residual update and commitment/codebook terms through this assignment path. Switches are explicit booleans as above, tested by checking numerical pathway differences, not by training ablations.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: training-only directed edges, item embeddings, per-layer residuals/code vectors and codebook. Output: per-layer code indices, quantized residuals and differentiable assignment/commitment values.

specification.text: For training interactions only, let N(i) be distinct next items after anchor i. Define S_ij=|N(i)∩N(j)|/(|N(i)∪N(j)|+eps), retain top-k nonzero neighbours per i (k derived as min(8, degree), no sweep), and let b_i=sum_j S_ij log(1+|N(j)|). For layer l with residual tangent vector r_i^l and learned linear map W_l, u_i^l=r_i^l+ (b_i/(1+b_i)) W_l [sum_j S_ij e_j/(sum_j S_ij+eps)]. Let x_i^l=Exp_0^c(u_i^l), and q_i^l=argmin_k d_c(x_i^l, Exp_0^c(c_k^l))^2. Use ordinary RQ residual update from the selected code in tangent coordinates. behavior_on=False sets S,b to zero; geometry_on=False replaces Exp/d_c with identity/L2. Both-on is the specified path. Fixed c=1, with standard projection to norm < (1-1e-5)/sqrt(c); no tuned constants. The shared-successor signal and curved distance jointly determine assignment and its gradients.

ideas.title: Successor-fork angular transport in the quantizer's Poincare tangent space

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: In code only, behavior_on=False replaces rho with the training median radius and zeros a_ij, leaving the curved mapping active. Do not train this arm.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The one formal run uses branch-derived rho and overlap weights with Poincare radial projection/geodesic distance. Train once only.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: In code only, geometry_on=False replaces maps, radial projection and distance by Euclidean norm scaling and squared Euclidean distance, while retaining branch-derived radii and overlap pairs. Do not train this arm.
ideas.behavior_computation: From Stage2 training interactions only, form N(i) as the distinct next-item set after i; branch count is |N(i)| and neighbour overlap is Jaccard(N(i),N(j)) for retained top-k positive neighbours. No validation/test interactions contribute.

ideas.cost_estimate: Train-only sparse graph construction O(E_k) and memory O(E_k). ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Branch count should encode uncertainty radially while shared-successor items receive a coherent geodesic neighborhood; if this structure is useful to next-item generation, SIDs and encoder gradients will change and the single Stage3 run will exceed test Recall@10 0.065. Record radial/count association, graph-neighbour SID predictability and Recall without using diagnostics as gates.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Encoder-to-quantizer interface: project each encoded item to its behaviour-derived radius in the ball, compute graph geodesic attraction there, then Log-map the same point into the representation read by RQ-VAE.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare Exp_0^c/Log_0^c radial projection and Poincare geodesic distance at fixed negative curvature -c (c=1).
ideas.key_change: Map the encoder output into the Lorentz hyperboloid, constrain its geodesic radius toward a radius derived from log successor count, and attract items sharing successor contexts by Lorentz geodesic distance. The resulting constrained Lorentz point is then mapped to the tangent representation consumed by the unchanged residual codebook; the graph attraction and radial constraint share the same point and encoder gradient path.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Freeze the successor sets, counts and sparse weights from the training split before training. The SID function is item-global and deterministic; Stage3 validation/test are only consumed by its fixed evaluation, never by graph/radius construction or optimization.
ideas.motivation: A branching prefix represents uncertainty over many next items while items with similar successor contexts should occupy compatible semantic regions; a flat latent space does not express both broad branching and shared directional structure in a single quantizer-facing representation.
ideas.novelty: It couples successor branching to a per-item radial target and successor co-context to a geodesic attraction term on the encoder output before RQ-VAE quantization. Unlike earlier behaviour-fork proposals, the mechanism is a calibrated radial coordinate plus sparse geodesic graph smoothing, not a branch-conditioned Euclidean supervision target or a residual/assignment reweighting.
ideas.observables: Encoder radial coordinate tracks training successor branching; graph neighbours become closer under curved metric and more predictable from SID prefixes; assignment distribution and gradients change. Decide solely by frozen Stage3 test Recall@10 > 0.065.
risks: Hard radial projection could erase useful encoder norm information; train graph overlap can be sparse/noisy; geodesic attraction may oversmooth popular branches; the normalization may still make the graph term too influential; Euclidean RQ over log-mapped points may fail to preserve curved neighbourhoods.
ideas.safeguards: c=1 fixed; clamp input norms to (1-1e-5)/sqrt(c), guard zero norms with machine epsilon; clamp acosh argument above 1; compute Lorentz/Poincare operations in float32; exclude empty-neighbour graph rows; detach only the loss-scale denominator; assert finite radii and gradients. rho is a count-derived nonnegative target, not swept or validation-calibrated.
ideas.spec_equations: Define train-only N(i), h_i=log(1+|N(i)|), rho_i=log(1+h_i), and a_ij=Jaccard(N(i),N(j))/Σ_j Jaccard for top min(8,degree(i)) positive neighbours. v_i=Exp_0^1(z_i); t_i=Log_0^1(v_i); v'_i=Exp_0^1(rho_i t_i/(||t_i||+eps)); y_i=Log_0^1(v'_i). L_graph=[Σ_ij a_ij d_{-1}(v'_i,v'_j)^2]/stopgrad(mean_batch||y||²+eps). Optimize baseline reconstruction+RQ-VAE terms plus L_graph; the normalized graph term is dimensionless and has coefficient 1 by construction, not tuned. Quantize y_i with baseline RQ.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: training-only edge-derived counts/overlaps, encoder outputs z_i, RQ-VAE codebooks. Outputs: quantizer inputs y_i, graph loss and standard SID indices.

specification.text: Use train-only successor sets N(i). Let h_i=log(1+|N(i)|), and let rho_i=log(1+h_i) (nonnegative, naturally scale bounded); for each item define neighbours j with positive Jaccard overlap S_ij, truncated to top min(8,degree), with normalized a_ij=S_ij/(Σ_j S_ij+eps). For encoder z_i, v_i=Exp_0^c(z_i) in the Poincare ball and its radius r_i=2/sqrt(c) atanh(sqrt(c)||v_i||). Set v'_i=Exp_0^c((rho_i/(r_i+eps)) Log_0^c(v_i)); this radial projection is differentiable and maps to target radius rho_i. Minimize L_graph=Σ_iΣ_j a_ij d_c(v'_i,v'_j)^2, then quantize y_i=Log_0^c(v'_i) using baseline Euclidean RQ assignments/decoder. To ensure geometry is necessary to the coupled pathway, define behaviour_on=False as rho_i=median_train(rho) and a_ij=0; geometry_on=False uses Euclidean norm/radial scaling and Euclidean pair distance on z. Both-on uses the above single curved point and graph loss. The radial target is derived from observed branch counts, no coupling weight: add graph loss as a mean per-item squared distance divided by its detached batch mean squared latent norm (dimensionless normalization).

ideas.title: Branching-calibrated radial targets with geodesic successor attraction

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Switch target construction off (α_i=0 and y_i=0), leaving the baseline RQ-VAE objective; this is a comparison definition, not a training arm.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use training-only transition-derived r_i,u_i and Poincare geodesic supervision exactly as specified; train this sole candidate once.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Replace exp/log and Poincare distance with Euclidean target r_i u_i and squared Euclidean distance; this is a comparison definition, not a training arm.
ideas.behavior_computation: In training split only, count adjacent item pairs (i,j) within each user's time-ordered sequence; aggregate outgoing counts and normalize per source item.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed, user-local next-item transition counts and successor branching distribution.
ideas.cost_estimate: One sparse successor-profile projection per batch plus one Poincare distance per item, O(B·nnz(profile)+B·D); at frozen scale 24,556 items/24 steps/epoch/3000 epochs, batch work is 1,023 distance evaluations per step and 73,728,000 total, typically under 5% step overhead; target profiles precomputed once.
ideas.coupling_equation: L_i=α_i d_{P,c=1}(exp_0(h_i), exp_0(r_i·u_i))²; r_i=R(1−H(p_i)/log d_i), u_i=normalize(Ap_i).
ideas.coupling_path: Transition counts determine both target radius and target direction; geodesic distance from the quantizer's encoder latent to that target supplies the gradient that moves the latent and therefore its code assignments.

evidence_revision.evidence_note: Positive row scalar changed 0 arg-mins (all unchanged; measured True); codeword-dependent weight moved 0 top-1 assignments (measured False)

ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If next-item predictability has a meaningful branching hierarchy, coupled radial/angular supervision changes encoder gradients and SID assignments to align predictable items with usable hierarchy; retain only if the single frozen Stage3 test Recall@10 exceeds 0.065.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Encoder-side behavior supervision during each Stage2 minibatch, on the latent representation immediately before residual quantization.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare exp map at origin and geodesic distance for fixed negative curvature c=1.
ideas.key_change: Build a training-only successor distribution for each item, then pull its encoded point toward a hyperbolic target whose radius is determined by branching entropy and whose direction is a weighted successor-profile embedding. Quantization continues on the same representation, so the supervision changes the assignments it feeds.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Build counts solely from training interactions before Stage2; validation and test events are never loaded by the target builder, and targets are frozen before Stage3.
ideas.motivation: Successor branching can encode how predictable an item's next step is: high-entropy successors should occupy a broad, near-origin region while low-entropy items can be placed farther out where angular distinctions are sharper.
ideas.novelty: Unlike existing successor-entropy curvature arms that alter quantization geometry/radial gating directly, this supervises the encoder representation with a per-item radial target and uses successor overlap to set an angular target jointly in one distance objective.
ideas.observables: Behavior-on changes latent gradients and code assignments by successor branching class; log radial latent norm, target-distance distributions, assignment changes, and final Stage3 test Recall@10.
risks: Sparse successor vectors may be noisy for rare items; radial target may merely encode popularity, and fixed projection may lose successor semantics.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp norms below 1−1e−5; use stable acosh(max(argument,1+1e−7)); log with p>0 only; use zero target direction when profile is empty and zero radial target; normalize with epsilon 1e−8; detach empirical scale and loss calibration; clip α at empirical percentile.
ideas.spec_equations: c=1; exp_0(v)=tanh(||v||)v/||v||; d(x,y)=acosh(1+2||x−y||²/((1−||x||²)(1−||y||²))). p_i from training adjacent pairs; H_i=−Σp log p; q_i=H_i/log(max(2,d_i)); r_i=R(1−q_i); u_i=normalize(Ap_i); L_beh=mean_i α_i d(exp_0(h_i),exp_0(r_i u_i))². Add L_beh to the existing encoder/RQ-VAE loss with its scale derived as the ratio of baseline reconstruction-loss median to detached behavior-loss median on the first training minibatch, then freeze that scale.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: training-only transition CSR rows, encoder latents h_i, quantizer and existing loss. Output: differentiable scalar behavior loss and updated encoder/code assignments.

specification.text: For item i let p_i(j)=count(i→j)/sum_k count(i→k), H_i=−Σ_j p_i(j)log p_i(j), r_i=R(1−H_i/log max(2,d_i)) for d_i>1 else 0. Make a fixed target vector u_i by normalized projection of p_i through a deterministic seeded random matrix A; target y_i=exp_0^c(r_i u_i). Minimize L_i=α_i d_c(z_i,y_i)^2, where α_i is normalized outgoing count, z_i=exp_0^c(h_i) and d_c is Poincare distance. Set R from the 99th percentile norm of the unregularized training latents, detached once after epoch 1; α_i=count_i/mean(count), clipped at its empirical 99th percentile.

ideas.title: Fork-conditioned hyperbolic shell transport

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Use deterministic random positive/negative pairs and constant aperture; comparison only, not an additional trained arm.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use training-overlap pair selection, entropy aperture, and Poincare cone scores in the sole run.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Replace ball mapping and cone angle with Euclidean cosine-angle containment; comparison only, not an additional trained arm.
ideas.behavior_computation: From training-only adjacent item transitions, normalize each source's successor counts into p_i; compute sparse overlap Jaccard-mass against candidate sources.
ideas.behavior_signal: Similarity of directed successor distributions between source items.
ideas.cost_estimate: Precompute sparse successor overlaps using inverted successor lists and retain top/bottom 16 candidates/item; per step evaluate two Poincare angles and two softplus terms per item, O(BD); 1,023 pairs per step, 73.7M pairs over frozen run, about 3–6% added compute and modest candidate-table memory.
ideas.coupling_path: Training successor overlap chooses positive/negative pairs and entropy determines aperture; Poincare angular containment scores those same behavior-selected pairs and backpropagates to quantizer inputs.

ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Distribution overlap reflects shared recommendation futures, and entropy-adaptive cones encode coarse-to-specific successor structure in quantizer latents; observable via changed assignments and Stage3 test Recall@10, retained only above 0.065.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Pairwise encoder-latent contrastive objective before quantization, whose gradients alter the vectors assigned by the residual codebooks.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare exp map and ball-model angular geodesic cone scoring at fixed curvature c=1.
ideas.key_change: For each source item, sample a positive source with high successor-distribution overlap and a negative with low overlap. Optimize the encoder latent so the positive lies inside a Poincare angular cone rooted at the anchor while the negative violates containment, with cone aperture set by anchor successor entropy.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Candidate pairs and distributions are generated only from the training interaction file, deterministically before training; no evaluation interactions are available to this component.
ideas.motivation: Items with similar next-item distributions should share a semantic direction, while items with distinct successor distributions should be separated; ordinary pairwise Euclidean similarity does not naturally encode nested specificity.
ideas.novelty: This uses sampled directed-transition distribution similarity as the positive/negative selector inside a hyperbolic cone containment objective, rather than behavior-weighted codeword assignment, Frechet residuals, or geodesic ranking of existing codes.
ideas.observables: Latent angular neighborhoods and code assignments become more predictive of successor-distribution overlap; record positive/negative cone violation and Stage3 test Recall@10.
risks: Top/bottom overlap may be unstable for sparse rows; angular cone semantics in the ball can be sensitive near the boundary; repeated sampled pairs can overfit popular destinations.
ideas.safeguards: Project ball points to norm ≤1−1e−5; clamp angle denominator to 1e−7; clamp cosine to [−1+1e−7,1−1e−7]; ignore empty successor rows; set β bounds from the 10th/90th percentile empirical first-minibatch positive angles, no sweep; normalize loss by valid pair count.
ideas.spec_equations: p_i(j)=count_train(i→j)/outcount(i); J(i,k)=Σ_j min(p_i(j),p_k(j)); β_i=β_min+(β_max−β_min)H_i/log(max(2,d_i)); z=exp_0^1(h); θ_c(i,k)=atan2(||z_k−z_i||,1−z_i·z_k); L_i=softplus(θ(i,k+)−β_i+m)+softplus(β_i+m−θ(i,k−)). Use candidate set of top/bottom 16 J values, cycling deterministically per epoch.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: train transition CSR, batch item latents and candidate pair table. Output: scalar contrastive loss and gradients to encoder latents.

specification.text: For items i,k compute J(i,k)=Σ_j min(p_i(j),p_k(j)) over train successor distributions. Sample positive k from top overlap candidates and negative n from bottom candidates using deterministic hash-based cycling. Map z_i=exp_0^c(h_i); define cone angle θ_i=atan2(||z_k−z_i||, 1−z_i·z_k) and aperture β_i=β_min+(β_max−β_min)H_i/log(max(2,d_i)). L_i=softplus(θ(i,k)−β_i+m)+softplus(β_i+m−θ(i,n)); margins derived from the median angular separation of a deterministic first-minibatch sample, frozen thereafter.

per_scorer_objection.scoring_1: The adaptive scale and loss-ratio normalization do not establish that the curved ranking adds value over an otherwise matched Euclidean ranking; the required switch controls are also absent.
per_scorer_objection.scoring_2: The loss-scale ratio of reconstruction EMA to fork EMA can become unstable or overwhelm reconstruction when the fork loss is near zero, despite the stated safeguards only specifying an epsilon for the distance MAD.
per_scorer_objection.scoring_3: The curvature is set from median encoder norm and fixed after an initial pass, but no matched Euclidean implementation or executable switch definitions are specified; the distance ranking may be effectively Euclidean in the occupied near-origin region.

per_scorer_rationale.scoring_1: Behavior 4: E5 audibly measures successor entropy and top-1 predictability across five bins, although it does not directly validate pairwise JS rank targets. Geometry 3: geodesic distances drive the pre-quantizer gradient (E12-E14), but no matched Euclidean comparison is specified and curvature may mainly rescale distances. Novelty 3: pairwise distribution-ranked geodesics differ computationally from the measured successor-geodesic-coarse and tangent-successor-residual arms in E6, but no traceable cited-work comparison is supplied. Downstream 4: encoder gradients alter the quantizer-facing representation, with prefix predictability/assignment diagnostics identified, but direction of Stage3 effect is uncertain. objective:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.

Continue the search for Stage2 RQ-VAE mechanisms that couple a training-only behaviour signal and an explicit hyperbolic operation on one connected computational path, judged only by Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065. The direction of this round comes from four measured rounds rather than from taste. First, the identifier geometry is not the lever: the four arms of this session scored 0.050001, 0.054597, 0.051220 and 0.049670, all at or below the frozen baseline of 0.055537, and the arm of this session with the best identifier on every single measure (L1 hard error 2.740 against 6.468, 3156 second-level prefixes against 7414, third-level collision 0.132 against 0.275, third-level refinement 3.279 bits against 2.176, raw collision 0.070) has the worst recall of the four. Second, the granularity diagnostics do not predict the recall: over the eleven distinct arms that have both measurements, the L1 hard error rate correlates +0.37, the second-level prefix count +0.05, the third-level collision -0.20 and the third-level refinement -0.19, so the earlier apparent law was an artefact of two historical arms and duplicated rows. Third, the two arms that ever beat the baseline, at 0.061404 and 0.062501, came from a different training recipe: they supervised the encoder's ball coordinates with the training-only behaviour-fork structure, where an item that leads to many successors sits nearer the origin and items that share a successor point in the same direction, and their matched Euclidean control scored the same as their hyperbolic twin, so the curvature contributed nothing over its control and the gain came from what the objective asked the encoder to represent. This round asks for that behaviour-fork supervision rebuilt on the canonical baseline: the training-only successor structure decides the radial coordinate of every item and the angular coherence of the items that share a successor, the curved operation is the metric in which that supervision is measured, and the two are connected in one computation on the representation the quantizer reads. The proposal has to state how the training-only signal is computed, where the curved operation acts, how the two are connected in one computation, what the behaviour-off and geometry-off comparisons are, and what the single frozen Stage3 run has to show. One candidate, one training run: no ablation arm is trained, no constant is swept, and no seed repetition decides anything.

papers.abstract: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. However, Euclidean embeddings not only suffer from inefficient packing and limited separation - due to their polynomial volume growth - but are also prone to codebook collapse, where only a small subset of codebook vectors are effectively utilized. To address these limitations, we introduce HyperVQ, a novel approach that formulates VQ as a hyperbolic Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) problem, leveraging the exponential volume growth in hyperbolic space to mitigate collapse and improve cluster separability. Additionally, HyperVQ represents codebook vectors as geometric representatives of hyperbolic decision hyperplanes, encouraging disentangled and robust latent representations. Our experiments demonstrate that HyperVQ matches traditional VQ in generative and reconstruction tasks, while surpassing it in disc

papers.abstract: Residual Vector Quantization turns continuous representations into discrete, multi-level token sequences. Yet most methods operate in Euclidean space, despite the coarse-to-fine structure of the resulting codes and the latent hierarchies present in many data domains. papers.abstract: Most high-performance block-coding systems for image compression, such as JPEG, have been designed for software or dedicated digital hardware implementations where the data are already assumed to be available in digital format. In modern CMOS photosensors, smart-pixel technologies have allowed the realization of basic signal processing tasks at the pixel level, in analog format before analog-to-digital (A/D) conversion. The elimination of A/D converters and implementation of block-coding directly over analog blocks of pixels in such sensors can be attractive both in terms of area savings and power consumption. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
papers.title: Representation Collapsing Problems in Vector Quantization

papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been shown to be highly effective in solving optimization problems in a wide range of applications. Such algorithms typically use gradient descent with backpropagation and the chain rule. Hence, the backpropagation fails if intermediate gradients are zero for some functions in the computational graph, because it causes the gradients to collapse when multiplying with zero. Vector quantization is one of those challenging functions for machine learning algorithms, since it is a piece-wise constant function and its gradient is zero almost everywhere. A typical solution is to apply the straight through estimator which simply copies the gradients over the vector quantization function in the backpropagation. Other solutions are based on smooth or stochastic approximation. This study proposes a vector quantization technique called NSVQ, which approximates the vector quantization behavior by substituting a multiplicative noise so that it can be used for machine learning problems. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. The design of block encoders, under the strong hardware constraints that derive from the A/D converter removal, has been investigated in this paper. We present a comparison of three systems in terms of rate, distortion and complexity, and present a numerical simulation analysis of their sensitivity to implementation errors. The conclusion of the analysis is that linear-transform coding vector quantizers outperform full-search vector quantizers and warping hyperbolic-tangent neural networks, in terms of performance, complexity and robustness, for a CMOS imaging sensor implemen
papers.title: Sensitivity analysis of low-complexity vector quantizers for focal-plane image compression

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
papers.title: Representation Collapsing Problems in Vector Quantization

papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been shown to be highly effective in solving optimization problems in a wide range of applications. Such algorithms typically use gradient descent with backpropagation and the chain rule. Hence, the backpropagation fails if intermediate gradients are zero for some functions in the computational graph, because it causes the gradients to collapse when multiplying with zero. Vector quantization is one of those challenging functions for machine learning algorithms, since it is a piece-wise constant function and its gradient is zero almost everywhere. A typical solution is to apply the straight through estimator which simply copies the gradients over the vector quantization function in the backpropagation. Other solutions are based on smooth or stochastic approximation. This study proposes a vector quantization technique called NSVQ, which approximates the vector quantization behavior by substituting a multiplicative noise so that it can be used for machine learning problems. Specifically, the vector quantization error is replaced by product of the original error and a normalized noise vector, the samples of which are drawn from a zero-mean, unit-varianc
papers.title: NSVQ: Noise Substitution in Vector Quantization for Machine Learning

papers.abstract: We establish stable quantum ergodicity for spin Hamiltonians, also known as Pauli-Schrödinger operators. Our approach combines new analytic techniques of mixed quantization, inspired by local index theory, with stable ergodicity results for partially hyperbolic systems.
papers.title: Mixed quantization and partial hyperbolicity
HQA-Rec: Hyperbolic Quantization Alignment for Citation Recommendation

When code vectors leave the ball, the clamped log calculation is not the inverse of the map used for assignment, so the selected code contribution and next residual do not correspond to the code point used to select that code. findings.reproduction: Set a codebook vector to any norm greater than 1 (for example, norm 2) with curvature 1. `ball_exp_map(0, code)` yields an in-ball point, but `ball_log_map(0, code)` receives the out-of-ball vector and clamps its atanh argument. The resulting tangent is not the tangent whose exponential produced the assignment point.

findings.correction: Compute `code_tangent` by taking the log map of `mapped_codes` (or, equivalently for this origin-based mapping, use the original tangent-space `codes`). Ensure assignment, selected-code reconstruction and commitment all use that same code representation.
findings.detail: Assignment compares the mapped codeword `mapped_codes = Exp_0(codes)` at line 296, but then converts the selected code using `ball_log_map(0, codes)` at line 305—as if the raw, unconstrained tangent-space code were already a point in the Poincare ball. The resulting `code_tangent` is not the tangent representation of the codeword used for assignment. Consequently, reconstruction and commitment use a different effective code than the one selected by the curved distance, breaking the intended coupled quantizer computation. It also creates a numerical hazard: raw code norms can exceed the ball radius, while `ball_add` at lines 91-95 of `model/hyperbolic.py` clamps only the atanh argument and still divides by the raw norm.
findings.reproduction: For any code vector whose norm is greater than 1, compare the current `ball_log_map(zeros_like(codes), codes, curvature)` with `ball_log_map(zeros_like(codes), mapped_codes, curvature)`, where `mapped_codes = ball_exp_map(zeros_like(codes), codes, curvature)`. They represent different tangent vectors; the first treats an out-of-ball raw code as a ball point. The toy smoke initializes small codes and does not check this assignment/reconstruction consistency.

findings.correction: Set `LOG_DIR` to `RESULT_DIR / "logs"` so metrics and launcher logs remain within this candidate’s promoted result directory.
findings.detail: Training metrics and launcher logs are written under the candidate source tree at `stage2_RQ-VAE/TIGER_fork-angle-transport/logs`, while the promoted candidate result directory is under `results/stage2_RQ-VAE/TIGER_fork-angle-transport`. This does not redirect the SID artifacts, but it violates the requirement that the trainer write only into its own result directory and separates the run logs from the promoted candidate’s results.
findings.reproduction: Run the trainer with `GENREC_SINGLE_GPU=1`; `_record` writes `METRICS_PATH` at train start and `_launch_via_torchrun` creates its log directory at train startup. Both resolve from `LOG_DIR` on line 77, which is outside `RESULT_DIR` on line 70.

findings.correction: Make the curved representation or distance participate in a differentiable training loss, in addition to using it for assignment, and ensure the resulting loss has a live gradient path through the intended curved computation. Keep the Euclidean control as the corresponding geometry-off version, and verify both settings’ losses and gradients as well as assignment changes.
findings.detail: The curved distance affects only the discrete assignment indices (`argmin`, or Sinkhorn followed by `argmax`). The differentiable quantization loss at lines 341-342 is Euclidean tangent-space MSE; it does not use the curved distance or the curved reconstruction. The computed `reconstruction` at lines 329-333 is unused, and the next residual is the tangent residual at lines 356-357. Consequently there is no differentiable curved-operation path to the intended parameters: geometry changes the selected code, but does not directly alter the loss gradient for a fixed assignment. The smoke test’s nonzero fork-map gradient does not establish that the curved operation contributes to that gradient; its own `geometry_off` assertion only tests assignment changes.
findings.reproduction: Hold the selected code indices fixed (or choose inputs where both geometry settings select the same indices). Backpropagate the reported loss with `geometry_on=True` and `False`: the loss computation and its gradients are the same for that fixed assignment, because the geometric distance and reconstruction are absent from the loss. The resulting gradient can still reach the fork map through the Euclidean tangent loss, but it is not a gradient through the curved operation.
